message.content:
**Beijing’s residential property market – snapshot (as of early 2025)**  

| District / Sub‑district | Avg. selling price (¥/m²) | Notes |
|--------------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| **Chaoyang**             | ~¥12,500–13,000           | Most expensive district; high demand due to business hubs & foreign embassies. |
| **Haidian**              | ~¥10,800–11,200           | Home to universities & tech parks; slightly lower than Chaoyang but still premium. |
| **Dongcheng**            | ~¥9,700–10,300            | Central historic area; older buildings, some luxury conversions. |
| **Xicheng**              | ~¥8,900–9,400             | Mix of old apartments and new developments near government offices. |
| **Fengtai**              | ~¥7,600–8,100             | Growing commercial zones; moderate price growth. |
| **Shijingshan**          | ~¥7,200–7,800             | Residential focus, less central, stable pricing. |
| **Tongzhou**             | ~¥6,800–7,400             | New administrative center; rapid development, rising prices. |

### Key points

1. **Average citywide price**  
   - Roughly ¥10,000–10,500 per m² (~US$1,350–1,420). This figure reflects both newly built units and resale transactions reported by the *China National Bureau of Statistics* and major real‑estate portals (e.g., Lianjia, Anjuke).

2. **Price trends**  
   - Since mid‑2019, Beijing has seen a gradual decline in transaction volume after regulatory tightening (price caps, purchase restrictions). Prices have stabilized around the levels above, with only modest year‑on‑year increases (< 3% annually).

3. **Regulatory backdrop**  
   - Local authorities cap sale prices at 120% of the “average market price” set each quarter.  
   - Purchase limits remain strict: non‑local buyers require two years’ residency plus proof of income; local residents face stricter down‑payment ratios.

4. **Luxury segment**  
   - Ultra‑high‑end properties (> 30 m²) in prime locations (CBD, diplomatic quarters) can exceed ¥20,000/m². These are typically sold through private brokerage networks rather than public listings.

5. **Rental vs. sales**  
   - Rental yields hover around 3–4%, reflecting strong demand among expatriates and domestic professionals. However, rental rates also vary widely—central districts command higher rents (≈¥70–90/m²/month), while peripheral areas offer more affordable options (≈¥40–60/m²/month).

---

#### Quick reference links (for deeper dives)

- [National Bureau of Statistics – Housing Price Index](https://www.stats.gov.cn/)  
- [Lianjia Beijing Property Reports](http://bj.lianjia.com/)
- [Anjuke Beijing Market Analysis](https://beijing.anjuke.com/market/)

> **Disclaimer:** Figures are rounded averages based on publicly available data up to March 2025. Actual prices may differ depending on building age, floor level, view quality, and other amenities. Always consult a licensed realtor or financial advisor before making investment decisions.
